en.headline: Development Bureau proposes new category for large building maintenance works
en.dek: Permanent Secretary Doris Ho said approval times for major maintenance projects are expected to lengthen, with a target of completing reviews within 45 days of full submissions.
body: The Development Bureau has proposed classifying large-scale building maintenance works as a new regulated category under amendments to the Buildings Ordinance, to be discussed by the Legislative Council's Development Panel on Tuesday.

Permanent Secretary for Development of Planning and Lands Doris Ho said on an RTHK programme that contractors would need to submit plans detailing temporary protection measures for Buildings Department approval and obtain Fire Services Department permission before work begins. Approval times are expected to be longer than previously, though the department aims to complete the process within 45 days after all documents are submitted.

The proposals form part of broader reforms following the Tai Po fire, including tighter contractor qualifications, interest declarations and direct disqualification for certain bid-rigging offences. Ho noted that costs may rise but fee waivers or discounts would cover about 80 percent of owners using support services.

zh.headline: 發展局擬將大型樓宇維修列新類別 審批時間料較長
zh.dek: 發展局常任秘書長何珮玲表示，大型維修工程審批時間預計較以往長，目標在交齊文件後45日內完成。
body: 發展局建議修訂《建築物條例》，將大型樓宇維修工程列為新的規管類別，立法會發展事務委員會將於周二討論。
發展局常任秘書長何珮玲在電台節目表示，承建商須向屋宇署提交圖則交代臨時保護措施，並獲消防處准許方可開工。審批時間預計較長，但屋宇署目標在承建商交齊文件後45日內完成。
有關建議是大埔火災後改革措施一部分，包括收緊承建商資格、要求申報利益，以及對圍標罪行直接除名。何珮玲指成本或上升，但費用寬免或折扣將涵蓋約八成使用支援服務的業主。
